32. Accordingly, in light of the aforesaid discussion, this Court unswervingly records and reiterates
that the Ld. Trial Court did not commit any illegality and/or impropriety under the impugned order
in so far as it directs framing of charges under Sections 469 and 500 IPC against the revisionist.
However, as aforenoted, no prima facie case or strong suspicion and/or reasonable ground exists to
proceed against the revisionist for the charges under Section 66C IT Act. As a corollary, the
impugned order/order dated 11.03.2025 passed by Ld. CJM, Central, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi, in

Crime Branch, is upheld in so far as it directs framing of charges Sections 469 and 500 IPC against
the revisionist and set aside in so far as it directs framing of charge under Section 66C IT Act against
the revisionist. Consequently, the present revision petition is disposed of in above terms. Needless at
this stage for this Court to further note that, though, it/this Court holds highest regard for the
